quick.summary: Why the second request in an email gets lost, and how to stop it.
quick.takeaway: One message, one action. Or say how many.

beats.line: I sent one email with three requests. Why did only one get done?
The first. The other two vanished.
Most readers act on the first ask, then file the message.
So I send three emails? That’s spam.
Three clear messages beat one that half works.
Give each a subject line that says the action.
Or one message with numbered asks?
Fine, if the subject line says how many.
Subject: three quick asks for you, by Friday.
Now nobody files it after the first one.

quiz.question: You need three different things from the same person. What works best?
options: One long paragraph with all three
The most urgent one at the end
A reply on an old thread
quiz.explanation: Readers tend to act on one thing per message; separating or numbering the asks keeps any from being missed.

quiz.question: Packing several requests into one message makes each one more likely to get done.
quiz.explanation: Readers often act on the first and file the rest. One purpose per message, or clearly numbered asks, avoids that.
